title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H4, the currentness and identity-sensitive roots
note: FIVE CURRENTNESS/IDENTITY-SENSITIVE ROOTS, THREE NEW CARDS, ONE BOUNDED EXPANSION, AND TWO LIMB-LEVEL HOLDS DECLARED IN THE PRODUCT ITSELF. REUSE-FIRST COLLAPSED FIVE ROOTS TO FOUR ACTIONS. AUG-0160 ('latest technologies to improve CII ratings') and the FAST limb of AUG-0211 ('latest technologies - FAST valves, OCC, WAPS') are the same examiner intent asked two ways, so they are answered by ONE canonical root, QB7_I#q10, which carries FAST as a named example rather than spawning a second card. That was the disposition the committed H4 identity evidence recommended and the live bank confirmed it: QB7_I already holds WAPS (q7), OCC (q8) and shore power (q9) as single-technology cards, so what was missing was the SET, not another member of it. THE MAKER OVERTURNED OUR OWN COMMITTED EVIDENCE ON TWO POINTS. The Wartsila service catalogue was opened rather than trusted second-hand. (1) The engine list is NOT RT-flex only - it includes RTA96C - so the committed note's 'applies to Wartsila RT-flex 2-stroke families' was incomplete and the card states the catalogue's list instead. (2) The FAST product page makes NO CII CLAIM AT ALL. The '5% CII improvement' in our committed evidence traces to a separate April 2025 press release about two Ulusoy bulk carriers, where it is claimed for WPLO + ICC + FAST COMBINED - not for FAST alone. The card teaches the attribution explicitly and makes over-claiming it a trap question. A SOURCE IS NOT ONE VOICE, AGAIN. Wartsila's own press release expands FAST as 'Fuel Actuated Sackless Technology' while its product catalogue writes 'Fuel Activated Sacless Technology'. The catalogue is the product record and the release is narrative, so the catalogue governs - the same preference SKILL section 8.2c already encodes for status chapters over narrative chapters. The card names the conflict rather than hiding it, because a candidate who meets the trade-press spelling needs to know which one to defend. THE AUG-0135 NEGATIVE SEARCH WAS WRONG AND THE RE-RUN FOUND THE ANSWER. Its adjudication recorded 'declaration of health|health declaration' as 0 hits and 'maritime declaration|pratique|quarantine' as 0 hits. Re-run against the live 759-card bank over MARKUP-STRIPPED CARD BODIES, the first pattern returns 10, including QB1_A#q18 and QB4_H#q9, both of which name the Maritime Declaration of Health explicitly. The original search was title-scoped and reported as though corpus-wide. The queue's own H4 evidence note had already spotted QB4_H#q9, so the record contradicted itself. NOTHING WAS LOST - no card was wrongly commissioned, because the India-specific ask is genuinely uncovered - but the evidence shape was unsound and is corrected here. THE INDIA HEALTH FORM RESOLVED TO INDIAN PRIMARY LAW. Not to a generic international MDH: the Indian Port Health Rules, 1955 prescribe it at rule 5, with the form at Appendix 5, and the rule was read verbatim from the Ministry of Health's own port-health portal. The load-bearing find is the SAVINGS CLAUSE: the Indian Ports Act, 2025 repeals the Indian Ports Act, 1908 at s.85(1), but s.85(2)(a) continues rules made under it 'till new notification, rule, regulation, bye-law, order or exemption is made'. Without that clause a candidate could be argued out of a correct citation by an examiner pointing at the repeal. TWO LIMBS ARE HELD IN PUBLIC RATHER THAN GUESSED. The commencement date of the Indian Ports Act, 2025 could not be verified in the Gazette - s.1(2) leaves it to notification - so the card gives assent 21 August 2025 and tells the candidate NOT to quote a commencement date. And MACN's own front page and third-party write-ups disagreed about which annual report is current, so the 'latest outcome' limb answers with DATED developments verified at macn.dk and explicitly declines to name an annual-report year. Both are recorded in held_limbs with what would unblock them. ONE STALE FIGURE CORRECTED INSIDE THE EXPANSION. QB5_E#q4 taught '150+ member companies' in two places; MACN's own site says over 225 members across more than 45 countries. The figure is corrected on the card AND on its cheat sheet, because leaving the revision layer behind would have had the corpus asserting two different membership numbers for one organisation.
examiner_relationship_delta_note: Zero by design. H4 authors cards and does not ingest examiner relationships; the examiner index and its 958 rows are regenerated as an H5 requalification step, which is where the handover already places examiner/index regeneration.

held_limbs.exact_unknown: The commencement date of the Indian Ports Act, 2025. Section 1(2) provides that it comes into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint by notification in the Official Gazette, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions.
held_limbs.sources_searched: The Act itself, retrieved from shipmin.gov.in and read - s.1(2), s.85(1) and s.85(2)(a) quoted verbatim from the Gazette text. A secondary encyclopaedia entry asserts commencement on 1 April 2026 with rules notified 21 July 2026; that is NOT a primary source and was not adopted.
held_limbs.why_unsafe: A commencement date is a dated legal claim. Quoting one from a secondary source in front of a Kochi panel is precisely the failure mode this corpus has been bitten by before. The answer to the examiner's question does not depend on it: the savings clause at s.85(2)(a) keeps the 1955 Rules in effect either way.
held_limbs.evidence_needed: The commencement notification in the Gazette of India, or an official MoPSW/DGMA statement naming the date.
held_limbs.how_the_hold_is_expressed_to_the_candida: The card gives assent 21 August 2025, quotes s.1(2), and instructs the candidate not to quote a commencement date they have not seen notified.

cards.topic: Technologies that improve a ship's CII rating, as a SET - the metric-versus-fix distinction under MARPOL Annex VI reg. 28 and reg. 26/SEEMP Part III, four technology families, and Wartsila FAST (Fuel Activated Sacless Technology) as a named maker example with its engine list, its 90% sac-volume and 1% part-load figures, and the correct attribution of the 5% CII claim to the combined WPLO+ICC+FAST package rather than to FAST alone
cards.adjudication_note: AUG-0160 was adjudicated GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION against 5 CII hits, all rejected as single-technology or metric-only scope. Re-verified against the live 759-card bank: '\bCII\b' now returns 92 hits over markup-stripped bodies and the nearest miss is QB1_F#q9 ('as CE, how will you reduce fuel consumption ... related to GHG/CII'), which is an engine-room SFOC/WHR/hull card that mentions CII only in its CE-relevance paragraph and carries no wind, air-lubrication, alternative-fuel, OCC or retrofit content. QB6#q1 and QB6_E#q1 explain the metric; QB7_I#q7/q8/q9 each carry ONE technology. The set-level ask is uncovered. AUG-0211 was PARAPHRASE_EXISTING onto QB7_I#q7 with QB7_I#q8 as co-target and its FAST limb carried forward as genuinely uncovered - 'sacless|sackless|fuel activated|fuel actuated|FAST valve' returns 0 against a bank where 'RT-flex|RTflex|Wartsila' returns 8 and 'sac volume|injector needle|atomi[sz]er|nozzle' returns 23, so the negative is credible rather than a failure of vocabulary.
cards.shared_target_note: One canonical root serves both occurrences. AUG-0160 asks for the set; AUG-0211 supplies three members of the set and adds FAST, which is uncovered. Answering them separately would have produced two overlapping 'latest technologies' cards.

cards.topic: The Apex Manual - DGS MS Notice 9 of 2014 s.6.2.1.1 fixes the name 'Safety Management Manual' and its required contents; s.6.2.1.2 and s.6.2.1.4 the cross-referencing that answers 'why apex'; s.6.2.1.3 MSC.1/Circ.1371 and MSC/Circ.1014; s.4.3 the supersessions; and the explicit warning that Tier 1/2/3 is industry practice and NOT the Notice's language; and, from DGMA's live Engineering Wing FAQ, the MS (Management for the Safe Operation of Ships) Rules, 2000 as the statutory instrument behind the Notice and the apex manual as a required DOC-application document
cards.adjudication_note: AUG-0193 was adjudicated GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION on a reported 0 hits for 'apex' across 738 cards. Re-run against the live 759-card bank over markup-stripped bodies, 'apex' now returns 6 - and every one is a false positive: QB5_I#q2 and QB5_I#q7 match inside 'CAPEX', QB7_I#q2 inside 'CAPEX', QB5_A#q14 and QB5_A#q18 are the apex of Bloom's taxonomy, and QB3_J#q5 is NOS-DCP as India's 'apex framework'. No card names the ISM Apex Manual. The pattern is demonstrably capable of finding the word, which is what makes the negative on the ISM sense credible. AUG-0194 ('why apex?') was EXPANDS_PRIOR_FRESH_ASK on AUG-0193 and is answered as a limb of this card, which is what its adjudication anticipated.
cards.shared_target_note: AUG-0193 asks what the manual is; AUG-0194 asks why it is called the apex. They were consecutive probes in one submission and are answered as one card with the 'why' given its own section.

cards.topic: The health declaration form used before arrival in India - the Maritime Declaration of Health, prescribed by the Indian Port Health Rules, 1955 rule 5 with the form at Appendix 5; the delivery chain to the Health Officer and pratique; the Indian Ports Act, 2025 s.85(1) repeal and s.85(2)(a) savings; and the FAL maritime-single-window channel in force from 1 January 2024
cards.adjudication_note: CLASSIFICATION UPHELD, EVIDENCE REPLACED. The original adjudication recorded 0 hits for 'declaration of health|health declaration' and 0 for 'maritime declaration|pratique|quarantine'. Both are wrong against card BODIES: the first returns 10 on the live bank, including QB1_A#q18 (FAL Convention, naming the Maritime Declaration of Health under IHR) and QB4_H#q9 (WHO certificates, naming the MDH completed by the Master). The searches were title-scoped and reported as corpus-wide. The CLASSIFICATION nevertheless stands: neither card answers the India-specific ask - no card in the corpus names the Indian Port Health Rules, 1955, rule 5 or Appendix 5, and QB4_H#q9's subject is WHO-linked certificates, not Indian pre-arrival formalities. This card is cross-linked to both rather than duplicating them.

cards.topic: MACN 'latest outcome' - a currency limb added to the existing MACN identity card, giving dated 2026 developments verified at macn.dk, plus correction of a stale membership figure from '150+' to 'over 225 members across more than 45 countries', and the technique of dating a perishable answer
cards.adjudication_note: AUG-0195 'Macn, latest outcome?' was adjudicated PARAPHRASE_EXISTING onto QB5_E#q4 with QB1_B#q9 named as the sibling. The live bank shows a THIRD MACN card the adjudication did not name - QB5_B#q8 - so the corpus holds three MACN cards, not two. CORRECTION TO THIS MANIFEST'S OWN FIRST ROUND: I wrote here that neither sibling repeated the stale membership figure and that this had been checked. That was FALSE, and I found it myself while re-verifying the claim I had just made. QB5_B#q8 carried '200+ member companies, >50% of global tonnage, active in 50+ countries' - a THIRD different figure, whose tonnage limb is not stated on any MACN page I could find. Shipping the expansion without touching it would have left the corpus asserting three different membership numbers for one organisation. QB5_B#q8 is therefore corrected in this batch to MACN's own figure with its date, and told not to quote a tonnage share. QB1_B#q9 carries no membership figure at all - that half of the original claim was true. QB5_B#q8 is repaired under its own record, CORR-MACN-MEMBERSHIP-20260901, because it is a shipped card this batch does not own.

dissolved_holds.was: HOLD_CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED - which MACN annual report is current
dissolved_holds.why: The hold was WRONG and independent review broke it. I checked MACN's front page and its news listing, found them inconsistent with third-party reporting, and held the limb. The reviewer went to the issuer's PUBLICATIONS INDEX, which settles it outright: the MACN 2025 Annual Report, posted May 2026, heads a list running back to 2016. I re-verified that at macn.dk before changing anything. The card now NAMES the 2025 report and, because the failure is more instructive than the fact, explains that two of the issuer's own surfaces would have left a candidate hedging and that the index is the one that answers.
dissolved_holds.lesson: This is SKILL 8.2c - 'a source is not one voice' - firing on an issuer's WEBSITE rather than inside a long document, and it is the same shape as the oralnotes/assets miss in the same batch: I stopped at two surfaces of a publisher and treated the disagreement between them as the answer, when a third surface existed and was decisive. A hold is a claim that the evidence does not exist, and it needs the same negative-search discipline as a GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION.

review_round_note: TWO ROUNDS. Round 1 was four independent clean-context reviewers, one per root plus a structural/governance reviewer. Every material finding was re-verified BY THE PRODUCER at primary source before any product change, and two reviewer claims were themselves corrected in the process: the successor rule-set named in G.S.R. 304(E) is the Indian Port PUBLIC Health Rules, 2026, not the 'Indian Port Health Rules, 2026'; and the oralnotes file number ENG/ISM/59(4)/97 is neither wrong nor unverifiable - it is printed on page 1 of the 2014 notice and is a standing series-wide DGS file number. THE FINDING THAT MATTERED MOST WAS A SOURCING FAILURE OF MINE. I recorded MS Notice 9 of 2014 as ACCESS_LIMITED after two hosts refused connections - while a 1.1 MB scan of the notice had been sitting in meoclass1/oralnotes/assets/ since July. I had grepped the oralnotes HTML and concluded the notice was not held locally. The mandatory local-corpus sweep must LIST asset directories, not only grep documents; a binary is invisible to a text search. Reading it produced three improvements no web source had given: the full 6.2.1.4 clause 'but not the other way round', section 6.2.1.5 on integrated systems, and section 8.1.1.5's own DOC-application requirement. Post-edit digests were repinned after round 2; the pins in this file describe the shipped state.
